samples.summary: New image-src gate silently turns every relative/app-hosted image URL into the `[image]` placeholder
samples.evidence: `isSafeImageSrc(src)` = `SAFE_IMAGE_DATA_URI.test(src) || isSafeUrl(src)`, and `isSafeUrl` builds `new URL(href)` with no base, so it returns false for any schemeless/relative URL (packages/core/src/url/index.ts:24-31, documented: "Returns false for invalid or relative URLs"). Docs images uploaded through the frontend are stored relative whenever `VITE_BACKEND_API_URL` is unset: `docsImageUploader` returns `resolveImageUrl(url)` which returns the raw `/images/<id>` path when `BACKEND_BASE` is empty (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts:12-18, :39). Such srcs are a real document shape (see packages/docs/test/model/document.test.ts:996 `src: '/images/test.png'`). Before this change `imageInline` emitted `![alt](/images/test.png)`; now `!isSafeImageSrc('/images/test.png')` is true and the export writes `[image]`, dropping the reference even though the frontend export explicitly passes `inlineImages: true` "so the image source is kept". Same applies to the href gate at markdown.ts:224 for relative hrefs.

samples.summary: `formatSourcePosition()`'s `+1` still reads the run *before* the selection when the selection starts at the end of a block
samples.evidence: `offset: normalized.start.offset + 1` relies on `caretInlineStyle` resolving into the first selected character, but that function falls back to the block's LAST run when the offset exceeds the block length (packages/docs/src/model/caret-style.ts:59-65). For a multi-block selection that begins exactly at the end of the first block (drag started at the end of paragraph A and extended into paragraph B), `start.offset + 1` is past the end, so the painter picks up paragraph A's trailing run — precisely the "copies a format the user did not highlight" bug the +1 was added to fix.

samples.summary: `pasteFormat()` reports `true` unconditionally after `saveSnapshot()`, even when the write touched nothing
samples.evidence: After the three guards it calls `this.saveSnapshot()` and `applyStyleToSelection(...)` and returns `true` without consulting whether anything was actually written. `applyStyleToSelection` can be a no-op (e.g. a `tableCellRange` whose cells resolve to nothing, or a range covering no text runs), leaving an empty undo step behind while the caller (`EditorAPI.pasteFormat` → `notifyStyleApplied()`, and the toolbar toggle) is told a write happened.

samples.summary: For a table cell-rectangle selection `getNormalizedRange` returns the raw, unordered anchor as `start`, so the painter reads from the drag origin rather than the rectangle's first cell
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:120-127 short-circuits cell-range mode with `start: range.anchor, end: range.focus` — no ordering. `formatSourcePosition()` therefore samples `anchor.offset + 1` inside the cell the drag started in; for a bottom-right→top-left rectangle drag that is the last cell of the rectangle, not the first, so the copied format is not the one the documented rule ("first selected character") promises.

samples.summary: px→inches→px round trip can shift margins the dialog never intended to change
samples.evidence: `toInches` rounds to 2 decimals (`(px/96).toFixed(2)`) and `parseInches` re-multiplies with `Math.round`. A ruler-dragged margin of e.g. 100.7 px seeds as "1.05" and Apply writes 101 px, so merely opening the dialog and pressing Apply (without editing that field) perturbs margins by up to ~0.5 px and creates an undo step.

samples.summary: Paper-size Select matches presets by width/height only, so a custom size with Letter's dimensions is relabelled as a preset
samples.evidence: `PAPER_OPTIONS.find(p => p.width === paperSize.width && p.height === paperSize.height)?.name ?? CUSTOM` ignores `paperSize.name`; an imported document carrying `{name: 'Custom', width: 816, height: 1056}` displays as "Letter", which the adjacent comment explicitly says the CUSTOM sentinel exists to avoid ("silently relabelling it 'Letter' would be a lie").

finding.evidence: `isSafeImageSrc(src)` = `SAFE_IMAGE_DATA_URI.test(src) || isSafeUrl(src)`, and `isSafeUrl` builds `new URL(href)` with no base, so it returns false for any schemeless/relative URL (packages/core/src/url/index.ts:24-31, documented: "Returns false for invalid or relative URLs"). Such srcs are a real document shape (see packages/docs/test/model/document.test.ts:996 `src: '/images/test.png'`). verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end. markdown.ts:250-251 defines isSafeImageSrc as SAFE_IMAGE_DATA_URI.test(src) || isSafeUrl(src), and markdown.ts:267-269 returns the '[image]' placeholder when it is false. core/src/url/index.ts:24-31 builds `new URL(href)` with no base inside try/catch, so it returns false for any schemeless/relative URL (its own docstring at :21-22 says so, and packages/core/test/url.test.ts:20 asserts it). Relative image srcs are a real document shape, not hypothetical: the backend mints them (packages/backend/src/image/image.service.ts:128, packages/backend/src/api/v1/images.controller.ts:74), the frontend uploader stores the unresolved relative path whenever VITE_BACKEND_API_URL is empty (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts:12-18,39), and the CLI explicitly documents handling "inlines whose `src` is a server-relative path (`/images/<id>`)" (packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:26; packages/cli/test/image-fetcher.test.ts:62). Both markdown-export entry points hand the raw document to the serializer with no src resolution first: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/text-actions.ts:44 (inlineImages: true, comment says "the image source is kept") and packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:129. So an app-hosted image that previously exported as ![alt](/images/<id>) now exports as [image], dropping the reference; the same over-broad gate at markdown.ts:224 drops relative hrefs. No guard, normalization, or caller-side resolution exists to make this unreachable, and no test covers the relative-src case (safety tests at packages/docs/test/serialize/markdown.test.ts:380-399,539-545 only cover javascript:, data:text/html, file:, svg). Content loss on a normal-use export path — in the correctness lane and blocking.
